title.narrative: Strengthening Integrated Humanitarian Response to Combat Acute Malnutrition Among Vulnerable Populations in Logone and Chari and Mayo-Tsanaga in the Far North region of Cameroon.

description.narrative: The Lake Chad Basin crisis continues to impact the Far North region of Cameroon, marked by ongoing challenges that lead to population displacements due to violent activities of the Non State Armed Groups, exacerbated by worsening effects of climate and competition for natural resources. This humanitarian situation has resulted in deaths, displacement, family separations, and significant loss of livelihoods for communities in the region. In response, this CERF allocation aims to enhance the humanitarian efforts by addressing acute malnutrition among the most vulnerable populations in the Logone and Chari and Mayo-Tsanaga divisions. These areas are particularly affected by the worsening nutrition challenges affecting especially children under five years old and pregnant or breastfeeding women. The initiative prioritizes lifesaving interventions to combat malnutrition in hard-to-reach locations while employing an integrated, multi-sectoral approach to complement existing activities funded by other donors, among them, USAID/BHA. The project targets the Far North region based on a comprehensive needs analysis that evaluated the geographic distribution of healthcare services alongside malnutrition prevalence. Goals include expanding service coverage, improving the quality of care, and providing timely interventions in critical areas. Specifically, under this project WFP will implement treatment and management activities targeting 16,352 children with Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM), while 1,860 pregnant and breastfeeding women will have their diets diversified, maternal health access improved through cash-based transfers and nutrition-related awareness activities. A total of 52,386 children under five will undergo nutritional screening. The project's comprehensive approach focuses on several core objectives: 1) Community-Based Interventions: Training and mobilizing community health workers to detect malnutrition early and allows for timely referrals of affected children to appropriate care facilities. By fostering community engagement, the project aims to create a sustainable response framework; 2) Nutritional Surveillance and Screening: Regular screenings will identify cases of SAM and MAM, enabling early intervention and reducing the risk of complications related to malnutrition. This surveillance offers a clearer picture of nutritional needs, informing necessary adjustments in the ongoing response; 3) Support for Health Facilities: The project includes capacity-building efforts for healthcare providers, distribution of nutritional supplies, and provision of essential medicines. These resources will ensure quality care for malnourished children as well as pregnant and breastfeeding women; 4) Promoting Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) Practices: Emphasizing the protection and promotion of IYCF practices in emergencies, the project focuses on educating mothers and caregivers about optimal nutrition for infants and young children.
